purpose: Reduce the development rejection cost of stricter speaker calibration
reason: On development speakers, frozen v2 three-recording FRR is 10% at 1.947% FAR; the first v3 choice has 13% FRR at 0.474% FAR
training: Eight recordings per existing training speaker; fit aggregate within-speaker covariance and global mean only from these 384 recordings
normalization: Symmetric inverse square root of (1-alpha)*within-speaker covariance + alpha*trace(covariance)/dimension*identity; center then transform then L2-normalize
selection: Minimum development FRR at empirical FAR <= 0.005; then lower FAR; then listed order (raw, centered, shrinkage 0.1, 0.5, 0.9)
test: The same 30 fresh test speakers; read cached test embeddings only after the new development selection is persisted; compare all candidates with frozen v2 one/three-recording thresholds
publication: Aggregate learned normalization matrices only; no individual training speaker vectors
stopping: Retain the selected development method regardless of test ranking; no further test-driven tuning
scope: Regularized WCCN-inspired cosine backend; not a reproduction of the paper's SVM/PCA system
